reason: Selected restart and history controls support conditional solution reuse in changing optimization tasks.

candidates.title: Recheck previous solutions before choosing warm start or restart
candidates.rule: When an agent revises an optimization problem, compare repaired prior candidates with fresh search, distinguishing identifier changes from genuinely disruptive constraint or resource changes.
candidates.passage: Earlier candidates remain useful after renaming or adding tasks.
candidates.finding: Across six Pareto sequences, MAPLE averages 0.879 hypervolume versus 0.868 always-warm and 0.824 always-full. Fresh search helps disruptive late changes; warm starts help renaming and selected low-demand additions.
models: MAPLE main backend not established in inspected sections
workloads: NLDO dynamic routing and cloud-placement optimization
candidates.conditions: Policies carry their own prior populations; targeted tests also use shared saved populations and paired seeds. Identifier mapping affects feasibility checks.
candidates.limitations: Six sequences and small additional controls; exact sign-test p=0.219 despite a positive bootstrap mean interval. Some targeted results use different reference rules and cannot be directly pooled. No universal change threshold is established.
candidates.validation_test: At each revision re-evaluate mapped prior candidates, then compare warm and fresh starts under the same solver budget; measure feasibility and quality on disruptive and cosmetic updates separately.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
